knowledge_point.title: Filling a Table of Values for a Parametric Curve

question.:question/problem:
Consider the curve with parametric equations

$$
x=2 t + 3,\qquad y=t^{2} - 2,\qquad -2\le t\le 2.
$$

Fill in the three blanks in the table. Give exact values.

Use the value of $t$ at the top of each column in the formula for that row. For example, $x(-1)=2 \left(-1\right) + 3=1$.

| **$t$** | $-2$ | $-1$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | {{field-2}} | $1$ | $3$ | $5$ | $7$ |
| $y$ | $2$ | $-1$ | {{field-3}} | $-1$ | {{field-1}} |
question.:question/worked-solution:
The missing entry is in the $y$-row under $t=2$. Substitute into $y=t^{2} - 2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}y(2) &=\left(2\right)^{2} - 2 \\ &=2\end{aligned}
$$

The missing entry is in the $x$-row under $t=-2$. Substitute into $x=2 t + 3$:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(-2) &=2 \left(-2\right) + 3 \\ &=-1\end{aligned}
$$

The missing entry is in the $y$-row under $t=0$. Substitute into $y=t^{2} - 2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}y(0) &=\left(0\right)^{2} - 2 \\ &=-2\end{aligned}
$$

The completed table is

| **$t$** | $-2$ | $-1$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | $-1$ | $1$ | $3$ | $5$ | $7$ |
| $y$ | $2$ | $-1$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $2$ |

knowledge_point.title: Filling a Table of Values for a Parametric Curve

question.:question/problem:
Consider the curve with parametric equations

$$
x=\frac{t + 1}{t + 5},\qquad y=t^{2} - t - 1,\qquad -2\le t\le 2.
$$

Fill in the three blanks in the table. Give exact values.

| **$t$** | $-2$ | $-1$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | {{field-2}} | $0$ | $\frac{1}{5}$ | $\frac{1}{3}$ | {{field-1}} |
| $y$ | $5$ | $1$ | {{field-3}} | $-1$ | $1$ |
question.:question/worked-solution:
The missing entry is in the $x$-row under $t=2$. Substitute into $x=\frac{t + 1}{t + 5}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(2) &=\frac{\left(2\right) + 1}{\left(2\right) + 5} \\ &=\frac{3}{7}\end{aligned}
$$

The missing entry is in the $x$-row under $t=-2$. Substitute into $x=\frac{t + 1}{t + 5}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(-2) &=\frac{\left(-2\right) + 1}{\left(-2\right) + 5} \\ &=- \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

The missing entry is in the $y$-row under $t=0$. Substitute into $y=t^{2} - t - 1$:

$$
\begin{aligned}y(0) &=\left(0\right)^{2} - \left(0\right) - 1 \\ &=-1\end{aligned}
$$

The completed table is

| **$t$** | $-2$ | $-1$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | $- \frac{1}{3}$ | $0$ | $\frac{1}{5}$ | $\frac{1}{3}$ | $\frac{3}{7}$ |
| $y$ | $5$ | $1$ | $-1$ | $-1$ | $1$ |

knowledge_point.title: Filling a Table of Values for a Parametric Curve

question.:question/problem:
Consider the curve with parametric equations

$$
x=\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{4}\right),\qquad y=\tan\left(\frac{\pi t}{3}\right).
$$

Consider the following table of values. Angles are in radians.

| **$t$** | $-4$ | $-3$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $0$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | $-1$ | $- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$ | $0$ | $b$ | $a$ |
| $y$ | $- \sqrt{3}$ | $0$ | $c$ | $- \sqrt{3}$ | $0$ |

Find the exact value of $a-b-c$.

{{result}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
The $a$ entry is in the $x$-row under $t=0$. Substitute into $x=\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{4}\right)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}a &=\cos\left(\frac{\pi \left(0\right)}{4}\right) \\ &=\cos\left(0\right) \\ &=1\end{aligned}
$$

The $b$ entry is in the $x$-row under $t=-1$. Substitute into $x=\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{4}\right)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}b &=\cos\left(\frac{\pi \left(-1\right)}{4}\right) \\ &=\cos\left(- \frac{\pi}{4}\right) \\ &=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

The $c$ entry is in the $y$-row under $t=-2$. Substitute into $y=\tan\left(\frac{\pi t}{3}\right)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}c &=\tan\left(\frac{\pi \left(-2\right)}{3}\right) \\ &=\tan\left(- \frac{2 \pi}{3}\right) \\ &=\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute the three entries with the signs in the requested expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}a-b-c &=\left(1\right)-\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)-\left(\sqrt{3}\right) \\ &=- \sqrt{3} - \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} + 1\end{aligned}
$$

The completed table is

| **$t$** | $-4$ | $-3$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $0$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | $-1$ | $- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$ | $0$ | $\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$ | $1$ |
| $y$ | $- \sqrt{3}$ | $0$ | $\sqrt{3}$ | $- \sqrt{3}$ | $0$ |

knowledge_point.title: Determining the Range of a Parametric Equation

question.:question/problem:
Given that a curve is defined parametrically as

$$
x=2 t - 3,\quad y=t^{2} + 1,\quad t\le 1 ,
$$

determine the range of $x$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Consider each coordinate separately.

For $x$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
x &=2 t - 3
\end{aligned}
$$

The affine coefficient is $2$. The boundary $t=1$ gives $x=-1$ and is included. The coordinate is continuous on the domain and unbounded below, so every value on the stated side of the bound occurs. Thus $x\le -1$.

Therefore, $x\le -1$.

knowledge_point.title: Determining the Range of a Parametric Equation

question.:question/problem:
Given that a curve is defined parametrically as

$$
x=- 2 t^{2} - 1,\quad y=2 t^{2} - 8 t + 5,\quad t\in(-\infty,\infty) ,
$$

determine the ranges of $x$ and $y$.

$x$ {{field-1}}{{field-2}}

$y$ {{field-3}}{{field-4}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Consider each coordinate separately.

For $x$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
x &=- 2 t^{2} - 1 \\ &=- 2 t^{2} - 1
\end{aligned}
$$

The square takes every nonnegative value. Equality occurs at $t=0$. The coordinate is continuous on the domain and unbounded below, so every value on the stated side of the bound occurs. Thus $x\le -1$.

For $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y &=2 t^{2} - 8 t + 5 \\ &=2 \left(t - 2\right)^{2} - 3
\end{aligned}
$$

The square takes every nonnegative value. Equality occurs at $t=2$. The coordinate is continuous on the domain and unbounded above, so every value on the stated side of the bound occurs. Thus $y\ge -3$.

Therefore, $x\le -1,\,y\ge -3$.

knowledge_point.title: Determining the Range of a Parametric Equation Defined in Terms of Trigonometric Functions

question.:question/problem:
Given that a curve is defined parametrically as

$$
\begin{gathered}
x=3\sin\theta,\qquad y=7\cos\theta,\\
0\le \theta<2\pi,
\end{gathered}
$$

what are the ranges of $x$ and $y$?

The range of $x$ is {{field-1}} {{field-2}} $x\le$ {{field-3}}.

The range of $y$ is {{field-4}} $\le y$ {{field-5}} {{field-6}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Consider each coordinate separately.

For $x$:

Over the full turn, $\sin\theta$ attains both $-1$ and $1$, including at permitted parameter values.

Multiply by $3$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
-1 &\le \sin\theta\le 1 \\
-3 &\le 3\sin\theta\le 3 \\
-3 &\le x\le 3.
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus $-3\le x\le 3$.

For $y$:

Over the full turn, $\cos\theta$ attains both $-1$ and $1$, including at permitted parameter values.

Multiply by $7$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
-1 &\le \cos\theta\le 1 \\
-7 &\le 7\cos\theta\le 7 \\
-7 &\le y\le 7.
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus $-7\le y\le 7$.

Continuity gives every value between the stated bounds. The coordinate extrema need not occur at the same parameter value.

knowledge_point.title: Determining the Range of a Parametric Equation Defined in Terms of Trigonometric Functions

question.:question/problem:
Given that a curve is defined parametrically as

$$
\begin{gathered}
x=3\sin\theta-1,\qquad y=3\cos\theta+2,\\
0\le \theta<2\pi,
\end{gathered}
$$

what are the ranges of $x$ and $y$?

The range of $x$ is {{field-1}} {{field-2}} $x\le$ {{field-3}}.

The range of $y$ is {{field-4}} $\le y$ {{field-5}} {{field-6}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Consider each coordinate separately.

For $x$:

Over the full turn, $\sin\theta$ attains both $-1$ and $1$, including at permitted parameter values.

Multiply by $3$ and translate by $-1$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
-1 &\le \sin\theta\le 1 \\
-3 &\le 3\sin\theta\le 3 \\
-4 &\le 3\sin\theta-1\le 2 \\
-4 &\le x\le 2.
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus $-4\le x\le 2$.

For $y$:

Over the full turn, $\cos\theta$ attains both $-1$ and $1$, including at permitted parameter values.

Multiply by $3$ and translate by $2$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
-1 &\le \cos\theta\le 1 \\
-3 &\le 3\cos\theta\le 3 \\
-1 &\le 3\cos\theta+2\le 5 \\
-1 &\le y\le 5.
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus $-1\le y\le 5$.

Continuity gives every value between the stated bounds. The coordinate extrema need not occur at the same parameter value.

knowledge_point.title: Determining the Range of a Parametric Equation Defined in Terms of Trigonometric Functions

question.:question/problem:
Given that a curve is defined parametrically as

$$
\begin{gathered}
x=-3\cos\theta+3,\qquad y=-2\sin\theta+3,\\
\frac{\pi}{2}<\theta\le 2\pi,
\end{gathered}
$$

what are the ranges of $x$ and $y$? Use $<$ or $\le$ in the comparison blanks.

The range of $x$ is {{field-1}} {{field-2}} $x$ {{field-3}} {{field-4}}.

The range of $y$ is {{field-5}} {{field-6}} $y$ {{field-7}} {{field-8}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Consider each coordinate separately.

For $x$:

Check the quarter-turn points in the parameter interval and its endpoint limits: $\theta=\frac{\pi}{2}$ gives $\cos\theta=0$ (excluded endpoint); $\theta=\pi$ gives $\cos\theta=-1$ (included); $\theta=\frac{3\pi}{2}$ gives $\cos\theta=0$ (included); $\theta=2\pi$ gives $\cos\theta=1$ (included).

The value $-1$ is attained at $\theta=\pi$.

The value $1$ is attained at $\theta=2\pi$.

Multiplying by $-3$ reverses both comparisons; translate by $3$, then write the bounds in increasing order.

$$
\begin{aligned}
-1 &\le \cos\theta\le 1 \\
3 &\ge-3\cos\theta\ge-3 \\
6 &\ge-3\cos\theta+3\ge0 \\
0 &\le x\le 6.
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus $0\le x\le 6$.

For $y$:

Check the quarter-turn points in the parameter interval and its endpoint limits: $\theta=\frac{\pi}{2}$ gives $\sin\theta=1$ (excluded endpoint); $\theta=\pi$ gives $\sin\theta=0$ (included); $\theta=\frac{3\pi}{2}$ gives $\sin\theta=-1$ (included); $\theta=2\pi$ gives $\sin\theta=0$ (included).

The value $-1$ is attained at $\theta=\frac{3\pi}{2}$.

The value $1$ is approached at an excluded endpoint and is not attained elsewhere in the interval.

Multiplying by $-2$ reverses both comparisons; translate by $3$, then write the bounds in increasing order.

$$
\begin{aligned}
-1 &\le \sin\theta<1 \\
2 &\ge-2\sin\theta>-2 \\
5 &\ge-2\sin\theta+3>1 \\
1 &<y\le 5.
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus $1<y\le 5$.

Continuity gives every value between the stated bounds. The coordinate extrema need not occur at the same parameter value.
